_comment: Copy to rutm.config.json (gitignored) and fill in real secrets. These are the shared settings applied to every RUTM08; the site name + label password are typed into the UI per device (no manifest CSV).
_comment_lan: Applied as the LAST step: the LAN interface moves to lan_ip and the device drops off 192.168.1.1. The tool renews the laptop's DHCP lease and confirms the device answers on the new address. The detection loop also watches lan_ip, so an already-moved router can be re-run (leave the label password empty — it is on the shared password).

ntp._comment: TEC-857 — the router's own time source. It is the gateway of the LAN the server sits on, so it addresses the server directly; the ntp_forward block below is a separate thing, for the OTD500 upstream that cannot. Written to BOTH RutOS time subsystems (the ntpclient package and system.ntp): the demo pair had ntpclient on Asia/Jerusalem while system.ntp sat disabled on UTC, which makes one device's own log timestamps disagree.
ntp._comment_verify: The server is on the assembly network and unreachable from this bench, so verification checks the configuration, not a synced clock — see docs/verification-rows.md.
ntp._comment_interval: Poll seconds, and on this fleet it is a RETRY LATENCY rather than an accuracy knob: a unit cannot reach this server from the bench, so its early polls all fail and the interval is how long it stays on the firmware image's build date after it finally reaches one. 60 is the floor the RutOS binary accepts, and polling costs nothing here because the server is on the local network. Do NOT set it lower: the binary silently substitutes 600 for anything it rejects, so asking for 30 gets a ten-times-slower poll (the tools clamp to 60 and warn). Stock RutOS ships 86400, and the stock servers 2-4 (time2/3/4.google.com) are deleted rather than left below ours — on an offline site each costs a failover timeout, which is fixed in the binary and not tunable, before the server that would have worked is tried.

wan._comment: TEC-857 — a fleet-constant WAN address, so the OTD500 upstream of this router has ONE identical NTP line everywhere instead of a per-site lookup, and a replacement unit needs no site knowledge. The gateway is the OTD's LAN address, fixed by definition. Off by default: switch it on once the bench procedure below is part of the station's routine.
wan._comment_bench: APPLIED LAST, after FOTA/RMS/Tailscale, because it is the step that ENDS internet on the bench — the WAN port stops taking a lease and starts waiting for a gateway that only exists at the site. Two consequences for the operator: nothing internet-dependent can follow it, and a TSW202 must not be on the same bench segment during the run, because 192.168.1.2 is also the switch's factory address.
wan._comment_dns: State DNS explicitly — a static WAN inherits no resolver from the lease it is replacing. Empty leaves whatever is configured.

ntp_forward._comment: TEC-857 — carries the upstream OTD500's NTP through this router to the real server, which it cannot address directly (the server is on this router's LAN, behind its NAT). UDP 123 arriving on the wan zone is DNAT'd to dest_ip, restricted to src_ip so nothing else uses it. The rule is named and updated in place, so re-running the tool never stacks a second copy.
ntp_forward._comment_zone: Verification also reports whether the WIRED wan interface is actually in the 'wan' firewall zone. It is matched by zone, so if the wired port is not a member the rule is a green row over a dead path — the demo unit's zone listed only the mobile interfaces.

_comment_internet: FOTA, RMS registration and Tailscale need internet, which a RUTM08 gets over its WAN port — plug WAN into a live uplink on the bench. wait_for_internet makes the tool poll until the link is up (up to internet_timeout seconds) before those steps.

firmware._comment: mode = fota (device pulls latest-stable from Teltonika — needs WAN internet), local (upload a pinned .bin from this machine), rms (defer — registered device upgrades itself on first RMS connect), or none. keep_settings must stay true: a settings wipe would reset a moved device back to 192.168.1.1 mid-run.
firmware._comment_standard: The fleet standard is RUTM_R_00.07.24.3 (TEC-861) — Teltonika's current Stable, published MD5 625873bfed7e04fcef3f343fc8e8c3f9. Pin it rather than tracking 'Latest': the RUTM family already ships 07.25.x, which is ahead of what the bench has validated. Set expected_version to match the .bin — it is verified after flashing, and a device already on that version skips the re-flash on a retry.

rms._comment_auth_code: Optional per-company RMS authentication code. Leave blank if you register devices via the API below — then they connect by serial+MAC without a code.
rms._comment_api: api_token must be an RMS Personal Access Token with the 'devices:read' + 'devices:write' scopes, and the account must have 2FA enabled (else the API returns 403). device_series is the RMS device family — 'rutm' for RUTM08; if RMS rejects the registration with an unknown-series error, try 'rut'.
rms._comment_pack: Optional license: assign a Management pack right after registration (the RMS UI's Actions -> Device -> 'Set pack'). Accepts the RMS pack type name ('management_3y' = Paid Management pack 3y.), a numeric credit_type_id, or a fragment of the display name. Leave empty to keep credit-based management. Needs the 'credits:read' + 'device_credits:write' scopes on api_token (on top of devices:read/write above). NOTE: packs cannot be revoked once assigned; the step skips devices that already carry a matching pack.

tailscale._comment_key: Either paste a single reusable auth_key, OR set mint_per_device + an api_key/tailnet to mint a fresh pre-authorized key per device via the Tailscale API (recommended).
